description: Defines the 'headers' the small/nano model checks off when it clusters a request into a task. The small model's job is ONLY to select which of these sections are relevant (e.g. request needs 'tabs' + 'dom_data' but not 'screenshots'); it never reads the full payload under a header. The decision model then receives the full contents of only the sections that got checked.

headers.label: List of all tabs
headers.description: Lightweight per-tab metadata for every open tab, refreshed on tab open/close/update.

headers.label: Filtered DOM data for existing tabs
headers.description: Extracted page text + interactive element list per tab. Populated lazily (on first request that needs it) and refreshed on navigation, not on every tick.

headers.label: Screenshots when needed for agentic workflows
headers.description: Only populated when a command explicitly escalates to vision (tier 3). Not kept in sync automatically — stale by design until re-requested.

small_model_output_contract.note: Strict JSON only — this is what the small model returns, and it is the ONLY thing that decides which headers' data gets pulled before the decision model call.
small_model_output_contract.low_confidence_fallback: If the small model isn't confident enough to pick a header or command, it returns selected_headers: [] instead of guessing. An empty array means: skip data retrieval entirely and forward the raw transcript straight to the decision model with pulled_data = {} — the decision model must plan from the transcript + command catalog alone in that case. Data retrieval never happens except when a header is explicitly selected here.
